enhanced.fullText:
The National Science Foundation (NSF) Sexual Harassment Reporting Term and Condition, effective September 21, 2018, represents a significant expansion of federal oversight regarding misconduct in federally-funded research. This regulation operates under NSF's authority pursuant to the National Science Foundation Act of 1950, as amended (42 U.S.C. § 1862 et seq.), and the Federal Grant and Cooperative Agreement Act (31 U.S.C. § 6301 et seq.).

The regulation mandates that all NSF award recipients, including higher education institutions, must notify NSF within 10 business days of any finding or determination of sexual harassment, other forms of harassment, or sexual assault involving Principal Investigators (PIs) or Co-Principal Investigators (Co-PIs) on NSF-funded projects. This requirement applies regardless of whether the misconduct occurred in connection with NSF-funded activities, representing a departure from traditional scope limitations.

Key provisions under 2 CFR § 200.113 require institutions to establish robust reporting mechanisms and maintain comprehensive documentation of all findings. The regulation defines "finding or determination" broadly to include conclusions from institutional investigations, administrative actions, criminal convictions, and civil judgments. Higher education institutions must report findings from Title IX investigations, faculty disciplinary proceedings, and criminal justice outcomes.

Compliance obligations extend beyond mere notification. Institutions must provide detailed information including the nature of the finding, investigation timeline, remedial actions taken, and impact on NSF-funded research activities. Under 2 CFR § 200.338, NSF reserves authority to suspend or terminate awards, require PI/Co-PI replacement, or impose special conditions based on reported findings.

Enforcement mechanisms include award suspension under 2 CFR § 200.339, termination under 2 CFR § 200.340, and potential debarment proceedings under 2 CFR Part 180. Institutions failing to comply face significant penalties including loss of current funding, ineligibility for future awards, and referral to federal law enforcement agencies.

Recent guidance clarifies that reporting obligations continue throughout the entire award period and extend to findings made after award expiration if they relate to conduct during the performance period. The regulation has been incorporated into NSF's Award and Administration Guide (AAG) and applies to all new awards and continuing grants issued after the effective date.
enhanced.summary: NSF requires higher education institutions to report findings of sexual harassment, other harassment, or sexual assault involving PIs/Co-PIs within 10 business days, regardless of connection to NSF activities, with potential award termination for non-compliance.
enhanced.requirements:
## Notification Obligations
- Report findings within 10 business days via NSF's notification system
- Include detailed investigation summaries and remedial actions taken
- Notify NSF of any changes in PI/Co-PI status due to misconduct findings

## Documentation Standards
- Maintain complete records of all harassment investigations involving NSF personnel
- Preserve evidence and investigation files throughout award period plus three years
- Document all institutional responses and corrective measures implemented

## Institutional Policies
- Establish clear procedures for identifying reportable findings
- Designate responsible officials for NSF notification compliance
- Train research administration staff on recognition and reporting requirements

## Ongoing Monitoring
- Conduct regular compliance audits of NSF-funded projects
- Monitor criminal background checks and disciplinary actions for PIs/Co-PIs
- Implement systems to track personnel changes and misconduct findings
enhanced.reportingRequirements: Submit notifications within 10 business days of any finding or determination through NSF's FastLane or Research.gov systems. Reports must include investigation details, timeline, personnel actions, and impact assessments, with ongoing updates required for any subsequent developments or appeals.
